dedupe_keys.name: us nationwide test of the emergency alert system and wireless emergency alerts 4 october 2023

description: This testbed and operations case covers the seventh national test of the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, run by FEMA with the Federal Communications Commission on 4 October 2023 under the IPAWS Modernization Act of 2015. A Wireless Emergency Alert went to mobile phones at 2:18 p.m. Eastern time and an Emergency Alert System message to radio, television, cable, satellite and other participants at 2:20 p.m.; for the first time the national EAS test was started through the Common Alerting Protocol, not over the air only. The FCC's report of June 2024, based on filings in its EAS Test Reporting System and on stakeholder surveys, found that 96.6 per cent of EAS participants received the test, up from 89.3 per cent in 2021, and 93.6 per cent retransmitted it, up from 87.1 per cent; participation was 81.7 per cent from 20,682 filings, with radio higher than television and low-power FM lower. It named operational readiness failures, such as outdated equipment and configuration errors, and uneven WEA delivery, tone and vibration. A RAND survey for FEMA studied public reach. Coverage: the United States and territories. Format and access: FCC report as PDF, FEMA FAQs and RAND report, free. Caveats: EAS results are self-reported; FEMA's own survey data were not shared with the FCC. Simulation uses: operational testing of warning chains, reliability of broadcast relays and emergency communication planning. Related records: the Hawaii false alert of 2018 shows the same chain failing, and FCC DIRS reports cover network status in disasters.
